Harmontide · a field guide to an inhabited world · volume II · the anurans

Bullywugs & Mucus Toads

Two frog-and-toad monster-girl lineages, now with twelve species: seven in the Bullywug family (the frogs) and five in the Mucus Toad family (the toads). They start from one shared body plan: Anura, the order every frog and toad belongs to. This guide defines that shared core first, then the first concept models.

Update 2026-10-20: every frog and toad species now comes in five colours (the bullywug and the cane toad had theirs already): bullfrog, tree frog, poison dart frog, glass frog, goliath frog, desert rain frog, mucus toad, fire-bellied toad, natterjack and Surinam toad, each with one rare colour.

The central similarity

Born in water. Bound to it.

Harpies are defined by the sky. Anurans are defined by water: every Bullywug and every Mucus Toad started as a tadpole, and every adult still needs wet skin. That one fact drives most of their behaviour, so it is the shared core both lineages build on.

  • One life cycleSpawn, tadpole, metamorphosis, adult. Shared by both lineages and every future species.
  • One needSkin moisture. Water, rain and mud refill it; sun, heat and the Nether drain it.
  • One toolkitA long tongue, a strong leap, a croaking chorus.
  • One difference that mattersSkin. Smooth frog skin dries fast and keeps Bullywugs at the water's edge. Warty toad skin holds water and lets Mucus Toads roam.

The life cycle (shared)

The loop mirrors vanilla Minecraft frogs on purpose: frogspawn, bucketable tadpoles, and a variant chosen by the biome the tadpole grows up in. Players already understand it, and it gives these two a hatchling-to-bond path the harpies don't have. One exception: the Surinam Toad has no tadpole stage. Her young develop fully inside the pits on her back and emerge as tiny, fully formed Surinam toads.

1. SpawnAfter a chorus night, a pair may leave a clutch in shallow, still water. Bullywug spawn is a floating clump; toad spawn is a long string wound around reeds and seagrass, like in real frogs and toads. Rare, like harpy eggs.
2. TadpoleTiny, aquatic, harmless. Can be caught in a bucket like a vanilla tadpole. Grows over a few in-game days; feeding it (slimeballs, kelp) speeds that up. Owl harpies and fish-eating mobs are its predators.
3. MetamorphosisThe tadpole crawls ashore. Two things are decided here: the variant, from the biome it grows up in (warm, temperate or cold, the same rule as vanilla frogs), and its keeper. A tadpole raised in a pond the player built treats that pond as home and the player as familiar. Its species is always that of the spawn it hatched from.
4. AdultLives on land, never far from water. Wild adults also spawn naturally in their biomes, so the life cycle is a bonus path and not the only source of the population.

Shared systems

Every system below exists in both lineages. The lineage only changes the numbers and the flavour, the same way species variants re-skin a harpy without changing the model.

MoistureA hidden value from wet to dry. Refills in water, rain and mud, and near a filled cauldron. Drains in sunlight, in hot or dry biomes, and very fast in the Nether. When dry, she slows down, looks dull and heads for the nearest water. Left dry too long she slowly takes damage and can die: any anuran dries out and dies if it stays away from water for too long.
The tongueA reach attack of about 4 blocks. It catches food (insects, small slimes, magma cubes: eating one leaves a froglight, like vanilla frogs) and pulls dropped items in. What she does with the item is the lineage's personality.
Leap & swimFast swimmers who never drown. A strong jump and little fall damage. Out of water they move in bursts rather than a steady walk.
The chorusAt dusk, in rain and right after rain, they croak with an inflating throat sac. Nearby individuals join in and settle into one rhythm. The chorus is how the player finds them, and a chorus night is when spawn gets laid.
Wetting as kindnessThe shared bond action: splash a dry one with a water bucket or water bottle, or build her a pond. It is the anuran version of feeding a harpy, and it plugs into the same affection system.
Cold sleepIn snowy biomes, or when it snows, she digs into mud or a pond bed and sleeps until it warms up (this is called brumation). Wake her early and she is groggy and grumpy.

Where the lineages split

Real frogs and toads are the same animal with different skin, and that is how these two diverge. Each row is a shared system; the cells say how each lineage turns it.

SystemBullywug (frog)Mucus Toad (toad)
SkinSmooth, glossy, often brightDry-looking, warty, earthy, with big glands behind the eyes
MoistureDries fast; stays within a few blocks of waterDries slowly; roams forests, gardens and caves, and goes back to water only to breed
MovementLong legs, big leaps, flashy jumpsShort legs: walks and makes small hops; digs into soft ground
HabitatSwamps, mangrove swamps, rivers, lily-pad pondsDamp forest floor, lush caves, farm and garden edges, riverbanks
TemperamentLoud, boastful, pushy. A bully who backs down the moment someone pushes backPlacid, slow, stubborn, sleepy. Hard to impress, hard to upset
TongueSnatches things to show off: items from the ground, a fish off a hook, the last wordPest control: eats insects and small slimes, which makes her welcome on farms
DefenceBluff and numbers: puffs up, bellows, shoves; a group gangs up, a lone one flees into waterMucus: slippery skin (hard to knock back or grab) and a bitter secretion that gives anything that bites or hits her nausea. Predators learn to leave toads alone
ChorusDeep bellow contests: the loudest wins the pondA long, low trill; she sings alone just as happily
SpawnFloating clumpsStrings wound through reeds
Wetting (bond)Needs it often; a player who keeps her pond full earns grudging respectNeeds it rarely; she remembers who did it
DangerModerate in groups, low aloneLow; only dangerous to whatever tries to eat her

Lineage profiles

Swamp & riverbankSocial · boisterous

Bullywug

HabitatSwamps, mangrove swamps, rivers and ponds with lily pads

TemperamentLoud, boastful, pushy, secretly easy to scare

Ecology & behaviourLives in noisy groups at the water's edge. Sits on lily pads, holds bellow contests, snatches anything shiny or edible with her tongue, and leaps into the water the moment a fight turns against her.

Player interactionStand your ground and she backs down. Keep her pond wet and stocked with fish and she becomes a loud, loyal pond-mate who shows off for you.

SpeciesBullywug (bullfrog) · Bullfrog · Tree Frog · Poison Dart Frog · Glass Frog · Goliath Frog · Desert Rain Frog

NameFrom the frog-folk of tabletop fantasy (Dungeons & Dragons): "bully" plus "pollywog", an old word for tadpole.

DangerModerate in a group; low when you meet one alone.

Damp woodland & cavesSolitary · unbothered

Mucus Toad

HabitatDamp forest floor, lush caves, farm and garden edges, riverbanks

TemperamentPlacid, slow, stubborn, sleepy

Ecology & behaviourWanders far from water, eats insects and small slimes, digs in under soft soil during the day and comes out at dusk and in rain. Her mucus makes her slippery and bitter, so most predators leave her alone.

Player interactionLet her settle near your crops and she keeps pests down. Shed mucus could be a useful material (a sticky ingredient, or a salve).

SpeciesMucus Toad (common toad) · Natterjack · Surinam Toad · Fire-Bellied Toad · Cane Toad

NameFrom the Monster Girl Encyclopedia. The source is erotic, so following the "mainly fantasy" tone rule, her mucus here is defensive and practical.

DangerLow; nausea for anyone who attacks her.

Cold ponds & mountain streamsWary · flashy

Fire-Bellied Toad (Mucus Toad family)

HabitatCold ponds, taiga bogs and mountain streams, and the Nether

TemperamentShy, jumpy, much braver than she looks

Ecology & behaviourHides her fire-red front under a winter vest, trills at dusk, and when threatened performs the Unken reflex: arches her back and flashes the red belly and soles. Carries a small ember lantern that glows in the dark.

Player interactionApproach calmly, keep a pond clean and cold, and offer insects, and walk by her glowing lantern at night. Startling her triggers the display, which is only a bluff.

DangerLow; the display is harmless to the player, and warns predators off.

Farms & warm wetlandsGreedy · toxic

Cane Toad (Mucus Toad family)

HabitatSugar-cane fields, warm swamps and farmland edges

TemperamentSmug, patient, always hungry

Ecology & behaviourSwallows dropped items and small mobs whole (they are gone for good). Squirts milky venom from her glands when threatened (Poison I and Nausea I). Spreads into new biomes.

Player interactionKeep her out of your crops; she eats pests but also anything else.

DangerModerate: her venom, if she is provoked.

Dunes & heathsFast · loud

Natterjack Toad (Mucus Toad family)

HabitatSandy coasts, dunes and heathland

TemperamentBrisk, businesslike, very loud at night

Ecology & behaviourRuns instead of hopping, faster than other toads and even at night, digs into sand by day, and calls in a huge chorus at dusk that carries for miles and draws other natterjacks to her.

Player interactionFollow the chorus at dusk; leave her a bowl of water on a dune.

DangerNone.

Rivers & swamp waterAquatic · motherly

Surinam Toad (Mucus Toad family)

HabitatMurky rivers and swamp water, always in the water

TemperamentQuiet, patient, protective

Ecology & behaviourNever leaves the water. Feeds without a tongue, feeling through the mud with star-tipped fingers, and carries her young in pits on her back, where they develop fully. They emerge as tiny, fully formed Surinam toads, with no tadpole stage.

Player interactionDo not disturb her in the water; leave small fish at the bank, and watch the babies swim off at a birth.

DangerNone.

Desert & fog coastTiny · grumpy

Desert Rain Frog (Bullywug family)

HabitatDunes, desert coasts and fog banks

TemperamentGrumpy, jumpy, secretly sweet

Ecology & behaviourThe smallest anuran. Burrows into sand by day and leaves only her eyes showing, drinks fog and dew off her woven poncho, and puffs into a ball and squeaks when frightened.

Player interactionLeave a water bowl or a bottle of water at a dune and wait for the squeak; a startled one is easy to calm. Bond by wetting, like the rest of the family.

DangerNone; the scream is a bluff.

RainforestWarning colours · climber

Poison Dart Frog (Bullywug family)

HabitatWarm, wet rainforest and jungle undergrowth

TemperamentBold, watchful, fiercely protective of her young

Ecology & behaviourClimbs trees and walls on sticky pads, carries her tadpoles up on her back, and advertises her poison with bright blue-and-black skin. She hunts with a blowpipe and darts.

Player interactionDo not hit her. Feed her jungle insects and keep her pond filled and she lets you near. A bonded one may share a poison.

DangerPoisonous to the touch: any mob that attacks her is poisoned (Poison II). Otherwise she keeps her distance.

Ponds & slow riversBossy · loud

Bullfrog (Bullywug family)

HabitatBig ponds, lakes and slow rivers

TemperamentDomineering, loud, big-hearted underneath

Ecology & behaviourClaims the biggest pond and defends it with bellows, chest-pounding and shoves. Wears trophies of what she has beaten.

Player interactionStand your ground or bring good food. Being shoved knocks you back but is not harmful.

DangerModerate: a heavy shove, but mostly bluster.

Jungle & mangrove canopySleepy · gliding

Tree Frog (Bullywug family)

HabitatJungle and mangrove canopy, trees near water

TemperamentSleepy by day, playful and skittish by night

Ecology & behaviourSleeps on a leaf by day with her eyes shut and her colours tucked away. Startled, she flashes her red eyes and blue flanks, and glides between trees on webbed hands and feet.

Player interactionLeave blossoms and leaves; she may glide to you at dusk.

DangerNone; the flash is only a startle.

Misty streamsShy · devoted

Glass Frog (Bullywug family)

HabitatMisty cloud-forest streams, under leaves by waterfalls

TemperamentShy, delicate, a devoted parent

Ecology & behaviourGuards her egg clutch on a leaf over the water, and peeps at dawn. Her translucent skin hides her until you spot her beating heart.

Player interactionDo not touch the eggs; protect them from owls and crows.

DangerNone.

Rapids & waterfallsSilent · immovable

Goliath Frog (Bullywug family)

HabitatJungle rivers, rapids and waterfalls

TemperamentSilent, patient, immovable

Ecology & behaviourThe largest of all. Moves stones to build nest pools, never croaks, and carries a boulder on her back.

Player interactionLeave offerings of fish at a rapid and keep away from her nest.

DangerHigh if you disturb her nest: she stomps, and she can lift the boulder.

Concept models

Added 2026-10-18. Twelve first-pass models, generated like the harpies (tools/anuran_lib.py on top of harpy_lib.py, one script per species) at the same detail level: 4 texels per unit, 85–125 cubes each. The images are renders of the real GeckoLib files, not separate illustrations. The MGE toad and monmusu frog were inspiration only; each species has its own concept. All use the humanoid face (decided after comparing it with the frog face, see below). All twelve species are in the game as separate entities, each with its own spawn egg (2026-10-18). Life stages (2026-10-18): spawn hatches into tadpoles (own models, water only) that grow legs after two and a half days into froglets (own models) and are grown up after five; the Surinam toad keeps carrying her young and they are miniature adults. Eleven tadpole and eleven froglet models, generated by tools/gen_tadpoles.py and tools/gen_froglets.py. Relationships (2026-10-18): any meat or fish is a gift that builds affection; at 25 affection a monster girl joins you at your bed, and after a full night she lays a day later: harpies a fertilised egg (about a day to hatch), frogs and toads spawn on the nearest water source (a still pond first); the spawn hatches into tadpoles (see Spawn, tadpoles & companions). The Surinam toad keeps carrying her young on her back instead.

The Bullywug family (frogs), by height: Desert Rain Frog (about 1.1 blocks), Glass Frog (1.4), Tree Frog (1.4), Poison Dart Frog (1.6), Bullywug (1.8), Bullfrog (2.0), Goliath Frog (2.3). The Bullywug is the family archetype (a swamp-ranger frog girl); the Bullfrog is the heavyweight pond boss.

The Mucus Toad family (toads), by height: Natterjack (about 1.25 blocks), Surinam Toad (1.25), Fire-Bellied Toad (1.35, 1.55 with the cap), Mucus Toad (1.45, 1.75 with the hat), Cane Toad (1.55, 1.9 with the hat). The two sheets are at the same scale.

Shared anatomyAll twelve share one skeleton, so one set of animation code can drive them: a humanoid face with pop-out eyelids, a tympanum (frog ear) behind each eye, a mouth that pops open, a tongue that slides out, a vocal sac under the chin, a belly puff, and webbed feet with toe pads.
Pop-outs, not scalingThe sac, tongue, belly and mouth hide inside the body and slide out through position animations, as the harpies' eyelids do. No bone scaling is used.
Shared animationsidle, walk, hop, swim, croak, tongue and sit exist for all twelve. Each species adds its own signature moves.

Bullywug — concept model

Tall, long-legged and loud. About 1.8 blocks. The family archetype: a leaf-green swamp-ranger frog girl. Inspired by the monmusu frog girl, but built as its own species: a pond-contest bullfrog with a swamp-ranger outfit.

Visual design

  • SkinSmooth glossy leaf-green with darker blotches, a pale yellow lateral stripe and a cream belly. Wet glints on every large face.
  • FaceHumanoid: big golden eyes with round pupils and sparkle highlights, brows, a small smug smile and orange cheek spots. The round tympanum discs stay on the sides of the head as frog ears.
  • Vocal sacA yellow sac hidden under the chin that slides out and swells during croaks and bellows.
  • Hands & feetSoft-padded fingers; long webbed feet with four toe pads, so she stands like a frog on tiptoe.
  • HairA teal bob with a bang between the eyes.
  • OutfitA lily-pad skirt of eight drooping pads, a woven reed wrap and rope belt with a shell clasp, a necklace of frogspawn beads (each with a dark embryo), three cattails strapped to her back, a pink lotus pinned in her hair.

Palette

  • Deep green #2e7c42
  • Cream belly #e4e694
  • Lateral stripe #d6e484
  • Golden eyes #e2a81e
  • Throat sac #f4b832
  • Teal hair #26606e
  • Reed #ac864a
  • Lotus pink #e0648e

Animations (built)

  • idle / walkA slight frog crouch, breathing throat, blinks; a short-stride waddle.
  • hopCoil, launch with the legs straight back, glide, tuck and land. Her main way to travel.
  • swimBreaststroke with a frog kick, body flat.
  • croakThe vocal sac swells in three pulses.
  • tongueLunge, mouth opens, the tongue snaps out and back, a gulp.
  • sitFolded legs, hands on the knees: the lily-pad pose.
  • bellowThe pond contest: chest out, head back, sac fully swollen, mouth wide, arms flung out.

Model facts & open questions

  • Size27 bones, 121 cubes, 256×256 texture, 8 animations; about 28.5 model units (1.8 blocks).
  • Filesbullywug.geo.json, .animation.json and .png under assets/harmontide/; generated by tools/gen_bullywug.py.
  • Should the skirt and cattails be removable outfit, or part of her look for good?

Bullywug colour variants

Five extra colour morphs of the Bullywug, texture-only: the same model, animations and outfit, with new skin, eye, throat and hair colours. Files bullywug_<variant>.png next to the default bullywug.png. Columns, left to right: green (default), golden, blue, leopard, marsh, albino; rows: front, three-quarter, face.

Variants

  • Green (default)Leaf green, golden eyes, a yellow throat sac and teal hair. Swamps and rivers.
  • GoldenA golden-yellow morph with amber eyes, an orange throat sac and auburn hair. Warm wetlands such as mangrove swamps.
  • BlueThe blue (axanthic) morph: turquoise skin, dark eyes and purple hair. Rare, in any wet biome.
  • LeopardTan-brown with big dark round spots, a white belly and dark-brown hair. Plains and meadow ponds and rivers.
  • MarshA dark, mossy, nearly black-green swamp frog with emerald hair. Dark swamps and dark-forest ponds.
  • AlbinoPale pink all over, a white belly, red eyes and white-pink hair. Very rare, in any wet biome.

How they are used

Like the harpies' variants, the colour is chosen once per individual from the biome she spawns in, with the blue and albino morphs as rare rolls anywhere. The biomes above are the mapping used in the game (AnuranVariants): the colour is rolled once per individual (at spawn, and for tadpoles when a clutch hatches), saved as Variant and never changes behaviour. Rare rolls: blue about 1 in 25 and albino about 1 in 40 for the Bullywug.

Bullfrog — concept model

The pond boss. About 2 blocks, the second biggest anuran after the Goliath Frog. Where the Bullywug is the family's leggy swamp ranger, the Bullfrog is a heavyweight: broad, stern, bossy and loud, with a bullfrog's huge ear discs.

Visual design

  • SkinMuddy olive with dark green blotches, a pale lateral fold and a cream belly with grey mottling.
  • FaceHumanoid: big bronze eyes under a stern lowered brow, a flat mouth. The tympanum discs are huge (bigger than her eyes, like a real bullfrog's) and carry gold hoops.
  • Throat sacA big cream-yellow sac that swells to a huge balloon in her roar.
  • HairA dark-brown mohawk of five spikes that lean back, and a short ponytail.
  • OutfitA pelt mantle and cape, lily-pad pauldrons, a trophy belt (a fish skull, snail shells and pike teeth) with a big brass buckle, a rush kilt and leather bracers.

Poison Dart Frog — concept model

New, in the Bullywug family. A slender rainforest hunter, about 1.6 blocks: glossy cobalt-blue skin covered in black spots, because real dart frogs advertise their poison with bright colours. She is poisonous to the touch: anything that attacks her is poisoned (Poison II).

Visual design

  • SkinCobalt blue with black spots on the legs, arms, belly and back, glossy highlights, and a pale blue throat sac.
  • FaceHumanoid: big dark round eyes with sparkles, brows, a small smile, and yellow-and-black stripes on each cheek.
  • ClimberBig round, glossy sticky pads on every finger and toe (the real species' signature trait) and a climbing animation.
  • HairGlossy blue-black hair: short fringe, two braids over the shoulders and a high ponytail through a red tie, with a macaw feather.
  • OutfitA leaf bandeau, a cord belt and a woven loincloth with macaw-feather fringe, a seed-bead necklace, yellow-and-black armbands. A bamboo blowpipe is slung across her back with a quiver of feathered darts.
  • PoisonPoisonous to the touch: any mob that attacks her in melee is inflicted with Poison II. She only uses it defensively.
  • TadpolesThree tadpoles ride on her back, because dart frogs carry their young up into the trees.

Glass Frog — concept model

A delicate cloud-forest stream frog, about 1.4 blocks (1.7 with her parasol), with see-through skin. The front of her body is a real window cut into the texture, through which her tiny organs show.

  • CamouflageShe is nearly invisible to mobs and players until they get close, and her beating heart gives her away.

  • OutfitA cobweb-silk shawl, a dew-drop necklace, a gauzy leaf skirt on a rope belt, and a leaf parasol on a stem strapped to her back.

Goliath Frog — concept model

After the goliath frog of West African rapids, the largest frog alive. The river warden: a silent giant of about 2.3 blocks, the tallest and heaviest anuran, who never croaks but moves stones to build her nest pools.

Visual design

  • OutfitMoss-capped stone pauldrons, stone gauntlets, a bandolier of river pebbles with a stone disc, a reed kilt on a rope belt, and a boulder carried on her back in a rope sling with two shoulder straps.

Desert Rain Frog — concept model

A Bullywug-family species, after the Namib desert rain frog (Breviceps macrops). The smallest anuran at about 1.1 blocks: a round, squat sand-pink ball with huge eyes and a grumpy mouth. She lives in dunes and coastal fog deserts, so she is the frog for the desert biome.

Visual design

  • BodyRound and squat on short stubby limbs; velvety sand-pink skin with tan freckles on back and belly. The belly plates let her puff into a ball.
  • FaceHumanoid: huge glossy near-black eyes with a thin gold ring and big sparkles, a permanently down-turned grumpy mouth, rose cheeks. Calm or screaming, she always looks cross.
  • FeetShort, webbed, with pale cream toe pads.
  • HairA short sandy tuft and curls.
  • OutfitSand goggles pushed up on her head (brass rims, glass lenses, a strap), a striped woven poncho with a fringe of translucent dew beads that she drinks from, and a pebble pendant.

Mucus Toad — concept model

Short, stocky and sleepy. About 1.45 blocks, 1.75 with her hat. Inspired by the Monster Girl Encyclopedia mucus toad, kept to the mainly-fantasy tone: her mucus is a herbalist's salve.

Visual design

  • SkinWarty olive-brown under a glossy film of mucus, with tan warts scattered over the limbs, shoulders and head and a cream belly.
  • Parotoid glandsBig tan glands behind each eye, with a drip of mucus hanging from each. The drips run slowly in idle and quickly when she is upset.
  • FaceHumanoid: heavy-lidded copper eyes under flat brows, a flat placid mouth and a dusting of rose blush. Always looks mid-nap.
  • HairLong, wet, clumped moss-green hair: locks fall over the mantle and down the back under the cloak.
  • OutfitA toadstool-cap hat on a cream stem, a shoulder mantle and a hanging damp-moss cloak, a leather belt with three jars of her own salve, a satchel, a leather apron and a bandolier strap.
  • Hands & feetShort unwebbed fingers for digging, thick legs and wide feet with a small web.

Fire-Bellied Toad — concept model

New, in the Mucus Toad family. A small, wary mountain-pond toad, about 1.35 blocks, 1.55 with her cap. A plain mossy olive back with black blotches, but her whole front is blazing red-orange with black mottling: a warning she keeps under a winter vest until she is threatened.

Cane Toad — concept model

After the cane toad, a huge, toxic, greedy toad that eats anything that fits in its mouth. The glutton, about 1.55 blocks (1.9 with her hat), in the Mucus Toad family.

Visual design

  • SkinDry brown warty skin with darker blotches and a cream belly mottled with grey.
  • FaceHumanoid: half-lidded gold eyes under heavy bony brow ridges and a smug, flat mouth. She always looks hungry.
  • Glands & venomHuge milky parotoid glands behind the eyes. They are bones, so they can swell and squirt venom. The venom gives Poison I and Nausea I to anything it hits.
  • AppetiteShe swallows dropped items and small mobs whole with the gulp. Whatever she swallows is gone for good.
  • OutfitA wide straw hat with a red band, burlap overalls with a patched denim pocket, a bundle of sugar cane on her back and a tin lunch pail at her belt.
  • Hands & feetStubby fingers and heavy webbed feet.

    Cane Toad colour variants

    Five extra colour morphs of the Cane Toad, texture-only: the same model, animations and outfit (hat, overalls, cane), with new skin, wart, eye, hair and gland colours. Files cane_toad_<variant>.png next to the default cane_toad.png. Columns, left to right: cane (default), olive, rust, grey, sand, black; rows: front, gulp, face.

    Variants

    • Cane (default)Warm brown with tan warts, gold eyes and milky glands. Swamps and farmland edges.
    • OliveA greener toad of wet ground, with olive-brown hair. Jungle and wet forests.
    • RustA red-orange toad with amber eyes and red-brown hair. Savanna and badlands.
    • GreyA cool slate-grey toad with silvery eyes and grey hair. Mountains and stony ground.
    • SandA pale yellow-sand toad with green-gold eyes and sandy hair. Deserts.
    • BlackA rare near-black toad with orange warts, orange eyes, silver hair and bright cream glands that look more toxic. Rare, anywhere.

    How they are used

    As with the Bullywug, the colour is chosen once per individual, by the biome she spawns in plus a rare roll for the black one. Gameplay is the same for every colour (Poison I and Nausea I from the venom). In the game this is done by AnuranVariants, with the black morph a 1-in-30 roll.

    Surinam Toad — concept model

    After the Surinam toad: fully aquatic, flat, leaf-brown, tongueless, with star-tipped fingers, and young that develop in pits in the mother's back. The swamp midwife, about 1.25 blocks, in the Mucus Toad family. She never leaves the water.

    Birth sequence, seen from behind: (1) carrying, with the toadlets wriggling; (2–4) the toadlets climb out of their pits one after another and swim off; (5) the pits are empty; (6) the idle_empty pose.

    Visual design

    • SkinDead-leaf brown with darker blotches and a pale belly.
    • FaceHumanoid: small, wide-set, beady gold eyes, a wide mouth, a flat head.
    • The youngThree toadlets sit in pits on her back (she carries up to three). Each is a miniature Surinam toad, with the same leaf-brown mottling, a flat head with beady gold eyes, splayed hind legs and little arms. Each is its own bone, so they can wriggle and leave one at a time.
    • Life cycleEggs are pressed into the skin of her back, where they sink into pits (the honeycomb). The young develop fully inside, with no tadpole stage, and climb out as tiny, fully formed Surinam toads. In the game the babies are the same model as the adult at a small scale: a baby variant of the species.
    • Carrying & growthShe carries up to three young at a time. They take five in-game days to develop before birth, and a baby takes five in-game days to grow into an adult. Eggs are only pressed into her back when another Surinam toad is nearby.
    • Star fingersLong, thin fingers with plus-shaped (star) tips for feeling through mud.
    • HairLong river-weed green hair with a sparse fringe.
    • OutfitA pointed dead-leaf hat, a leaf-litter poncho, river-weed ribbons, a pearl pendant and a net bag with a fish in it.
    • No tongueSurinam toads have none: she feeds by sucking prey in. The shared tongue animation only opens her mouth and gulps.

      Humanoid face comparison

      Added 2026-10-18. The first three models with the frog face (bulging eyes on top) against the same models with a human-style face. Only the head changed. Decision: humanoid faces are the default for the whole family; the frog-face versions can still be built with --frog-face.

      Columns: Desert Rain Frog, Mucus Toad, Bullywug. Rows: frog face (full body), humanoid face (full body), frog face (close-up), humanoid face (close-up).

      What changes

      • EyesThe bulging eye cubes on top of the head are gone. Round, high-set eyes are painted on the front of the face, with brows, a lash flick and sparkle highlights, so they read like the harpies' eyes.
      • MouthThe wide frog mouth and the pale jaw become a small mouth with a lower lip, and there is a tiny nose. The pop-out mouth plate shrinks to match.
      • HeadTaller and squarer, like a harpy head, with a hair fringe across the forehead instead of bare skin.
      • KeptThe tympanum discs, so the ears still say “frog”; the glands, hat and goggles; the vocal sac, tongue and belly puff.

      What it costs and what to look at

      • SilhouetteThe frog read comes mostly from the bulging eyes and the wide mouth. Without them the Bullywug and the rain frog look more like a person in green skin; the toad survives best, thanks to the glands, warts and heavy lids.
      • ExpressionHumanoid faces make them friendlier and easier to read, but they lose the grumpy, bluffing character (the rain frog’s scowl, the Bullywug’s smug grin).
      • Throat sacIt pops out in front of the lower face, so on the humanoid heads it covers the mouth during a croak.
      • FilesHumanoid is now what python tools/gen_<species>.py writes; --frog-face writes *_frogface files instead. The sheet is made by tools/anuran_face_compare.py.

      Ties to the harpies

      One world, one food web. These are small hooks, not new systems.

      Owl harpyThe field guide already lists frogs as owl prey. Owls hunt tadpoles and Bullywugs at night, but learn to avoid Mucus Toads after one bitter bite.
      Crow & seagullFellow thieves. A Bullywug with a stolen item and a crow harpy who wants it could be a fun ambient scene.
      Shared codeThe affection, home position and synced-action plumbing in AbstractHarpy fits here too, as a shared parent or a sibling AbstractAnuran. Vanilla Frog and Tadpole already have tongue, variant and growth code to learn from.

      Species to come

      Not designed yet. Real animals that could become species later, listed only so the shared core leaves room for them.

      Bullywug family

      • BuiltBullywug, Bullfrog, Tree Frog, Poison Dart Frog, Glass Frog, Goliath Frog, Desert Rain Frog.
      • Later ideasWood frog (freezes in winter), Pacman frog (an ambusher that waits buried), waxy monkey tree frog.

      Mucus Toad family

      • BuiltMucus Toad, Fire-Bellied Toad, Cane Toad, Natterjack Toad, Surinam Toad.
      • Later ideasSpadefoot toad (a digger that sleeps for years), Couch's spadefoot, midwife toad (the father carries the eggs), marine toad variants.

      Design decisions log

      Added 2026-10-18.

      BriefTwo frog-creature lineages, the Bullywug and the Mucus Toad, in the spirit of the harpy guide. Each will get species like the harpies did; for now the focus is on what they have in common.
      InterpretationThe central similarity is read as the amphibian life cycle plus the need for water, with skin as the one axis where the lineages split. This is a proposal, not a decision.
      Follow-up, same dayThe Desert Rain Frog joins the Bullywug family. First-pass concept models for all three species were built from a shared anuran skeleton, using the MGE mucus toad and monmusu bullywug images as inspiration only.
      Humanoid facesAfter comparing frog and humanoid faces (see the comparison above), the humanoid face is the default for all species. Poison Dart Frog (Bullywug family) and Fire-Bellied Toad (Mucus Toad family) were added as the next species, each with its own concept.
      Decisions, 2026-10-18 (later)Poison Dart Frog: poisonous to the touch, so any mob that attacks her gets Poison II. Fire-Bellied Toad: the lantern glows in the dark (glow mask done), and she also lives in the Nether, which suits her name. The Bullywug family now has seven species: Bullywug, Bullfrog, Tree Frog, Poison Dart Frog, Glass Frog, Goliath Frog and Desert Rain Frog.
      Decisions, 2026-10-18 (latest)Goliath Frog: the stomp knocks back nearby mobs and the player. Fire-Bellied Toad: the lantern also gives off a light level. Glass Frog: nearly invisible to mobs and players until they get close. Added the Mucus Toad family species Cane Toad, Natterjack and Surinam Toad, so the family now has five and the whole anuran set has twelve.
      Decisions, 2026-10-18 (follow-up)Cane Toad: her venom gives Poison I and Nausea I. Natterjack: faster than other toads, also at night, and her chorus draws other natterjacks. Surinam Toad: fully aquatic. Her young develop fully inside the pits on her back and emerge fully formed as miniature Surinam toads (a baby variant of the same model at a smaller scale, no tadpole stage), supported by the new brood, birth and idle_empty animations and three separate toadlet bones.
      Decisions, 2026-10-18 (answers to the open questions)The central similarity is the life cycle and water. Wildlife with a pond pecking order, not a society. A raised tadpole takes the spawn’s species. The mod is to be named Harmontide. Any anuran slowly dries out and dies if kept dry too long. Cane Toad: swallows dropped items and small mobs, which are gone for good. Surinam Toad: carries three young, which take five in-game days to develop; a baby takes five in-game days to grow up; eggs need another Surinam toad nearby.
      ToneSame rule as the harpies: mainly fantasy. The Mucus Toad's erotic source material is reworked into defensive, practical mucus.

      Open questions, answered

      • The central similarityThe life cycle and the need for water: confirmed.
      • Wildlife or tribeWildlife with a pecking order (the loudest wins the pond), not a whole society.
      • Raised tadpolesA player-raised tadpole always becomes the species of the spawn it hatched from.
      • Mod nameThe mod will be called Harmontide. Its id is harmontide (renamed from harpies on 2026-10-18).
      • Drying outIt slowly hurts and eventually kills any anuran left dry for too long.
      • New: the Fire-Bellied Toad lives in the Nether, where moisture drains very fast. Is she exempt from drying out there, or does the Nether need water sources for her?

      Relationships (shared by every family)

      Updated 2026-10-19. Every Harmontide family uses the same relationship core; each volume only changes how trust is won, what she gives back and how she bears young. The other families (volumes III to XIX) are in their own guides.

      AffectionEach monster girl remembers every player separately. Feeding, petting and her family's own bond action raise it; hurting her lowers it. /harmontide bonds lists everyone nearby.
      SitRight-click any monster girl with a plain stick to make her sit; again to let her get up.
      Sharing a bedAt high friendship (25) she may join you in bed: once a night she decides, one in three at 25, certain at 100. Sleep through the night and she is expecting.
      ExpectingA pregnancy lasts one in-game day. Her belly rounds out as it goes on (the model shows it).
      Born devotedHer young are born devoted to the player who fathered them (full affection) and never share that player's bed.
      PresentsAt high friendship every family brings presents of its own kind.
      BondAffectionWhat it means
      Wild0Keeps her distance; her species' instincts decide everything.
      Curious3+Lets you come close and watches what you do.
      Fond10+Follows you a little way, accepts petting, stops fleeing.
      High friendship25+May join you in bed at night (one night in three, more the fonder she is) and brings presents.
      Devoted60+The family's devoted perk unlocks (see each guide).
      Full devotion100The most there is. Every daughter feels this for the player who fathered her.

      Spawn, tadpoles & companions

      Updated 2026-10-19. What a frog or toad does once you have won her over. All of this is in the game.

      Mating & spawn

      • BedAt high friendship (25) she may hop into your bed and sit snug beside you (one night in three at 25, every night at 100). Sleep through the night and she is expecting.
      • ExpectingOne in-game day. Her belly rounds out as the day goes on (her belly bone swells).
      • SpawnShe lays her spawn in the nearest water source: a still pond if there is one, otherwise any source block with open air above.
      • Tadpoles & frogletsThe spawn hatches into two to four tadpoles of her species, coloured for the pond they hatch in. They grow legs after two and a half days (froglets) and are grown up after five.
      • Born devotedEvery tadpole is devoted to the player who fathered the spawn (full affection) and never shares that player's bed. The Surinam toad still carries her young on her back instead.

      Companions

      • SitRight-click any frog or toad with a stick: she sits down until you do it again (tadpoles excepted).
      • BullywugEvery five to ten minutes she sheds a slime ball (only the bullywug herself, not the rest of her family).
